seo.title: Compare Melusina vs SaaS Sprawl
seo.description: See how Melusina's app isolation, private AI, and multi-keyholder security compare to traditional platforms where your data is scattered across dozens of services.
seo.keywords: melusina comparison, self-hosted vs saas, app isolation, data sovereignty, private AI, multi-keyholder

hero.heading: Your data in one place you control vs. scattered across 47 services
hero.subtitle: See how Melusina's isolation, private AI, multi-keyholder security, and verifiable trust chain compare to the SaaS platforms where your data currently lives.

comparison.heading: Melusina vs. the way things work now
comparison.subtitle: Every row is something you currently trust a vendor to get right. With Melusina, you don't have to trust anyone.

items.label: Data Location
items.before: Your data lives on someone else's servers. You trust that they won't peek, sell it, or get breached.
items.after: Your hardware. Your containers. Your jurisdiction. Nobody else has access unless you grant it.

items.label: App Isolation
items.before: All your apps share the same database and network. A bug in one can expose everything.
items.after: Every app runs in its own isolated container with its own storage. One app can never see another's data.

items.label: AI Privacy
items.before: Cloud API calls. Your prompts become someone else's training data. Your sensitive questions leave your network.
items.after: Private AI that runs locally in isolated containers. Your prompts never leave your server. Your data never trains someone else's model.

items.label: Data Portability
items.before: Try exporting from Notion or migrating from Google Workspace. Vendor lock-in by design.
items.after: Export everything in standard formats. Leave anytime. Your data is yours, not ours.

items.label: Key Management
items.before: One admin password rules everything. That person is your single point of failure.
items.after: Multiple keyholders needed. No single person can access the vault, decrypt backups, or lock everyone out.

items.label: Admin Revocation
items.before: Someone leaves the team. Revoke access across 12 different services and hope you didn't miss one.
items.after: Freeze their Admin NFT — access revoked everywhere in the same block. One action. Done.

items.label: Connection Control
items.before: Connect Zapier to Stripe. Now Zapier sees all your Stripe data forever. Blanket permissions.
items.after: Apps request specific capabilities from specific instances. You approve each one. Revoke anytime. Nothing is blanket.

items.label: License Verification
items.before: A PDF in someone's inbox. No one can independently verify it's real.
items.after: An NFT on Solana. Anyone walks the chain: License → Reseller → Foundation. Publicly verifiable.

items.label: Code Authenticity
items.before: The vendor says 'trust us, it's the real code.' You have no way to check.
items.after: Foundation-signed release hash. Verified automatically at every boot. Tampered code won't start.

items.label: TLS Security
items.before: A CA-issued certificate. Compromised CA = man-in-the-middle. Internal traffic often unencrypted.
items.after: TLS pinned in signed DNS records. Internal encryption between all containers. Verifiable by anyone.

items.label: Backup Security
items.before: Encryption key stored somewhere. Maybe in a safe. Maybe in someone's head.
items.after: Key split across multiple keyholders. Each share encrypted to its owner. Nothing stored centrally.

items.label: Boot Security
items.before: Machine starts, services start. No verification of anything.
items.after: 4-phase verified boot: check license → start monitoring → keyholder approval → start services.

items.label: Audit Trail
items.before: Log files on the server. Anyone with admin access can tamper with them.
items.after: Solana Memo transactions. Immutable. Verifiable by anyone. Can't be edited after the fact.

items.label: Notifications
items.before: Rich push with full message content. Every notification leaks data through the push provider.
items.after: Content-free pushes — payloads are empty. 'Something happened.' No data leakage through the provider.

items.label: Authentication
items.before: Username/password or OAuth. Another credential to manage. Another thing to breach.
items.after: Solana wallet login with three fallbacks: browser extension, mobile app, QR code. No passwords.

items.label: Inter-App Communication
items.before: REST APIs with API keys. Blanket permissions. No type safety.
items.after: Type-safe protocol designed by the creator of Protocol Buffers. Capability-based. No blanket permissions.

items.label: Sharing
items.before: Permanent share links. No expiry. No usage tracking. Once shared, shared forever.
items.after: Four modes: burn-after-reading, timed, use-count, unlimited. You choose how long access lasts.

items.label: Resource Control
items.before: Per-seat SaaS pricing. Usage invisible until the monthly invoice. No way to set limits.
items.after: Per-container spending limits. Real-time metering. You set budgets. Runaway costs are impossible.

items.label: Device Access
items.before: Download the iOS app. Download the Android app. Download the desktop app. Three stores. Three approval processes. Three gatekeepers.
items.after: Melusina runs on your server. You open it in any browser — laptop, phone, tablet. Add it to your home screen for instant access. No app store. No gatekeeper.

items.label: Building Workflows
items.before: Hire a developer to connect Typeform to Airtable to Zapier to Slack. Hope none of them change their API.
items.after: Drag process steps into a pipeline. Terms → verification → document upload → review → approval. Each step is a Pearl. Each respondent gets their own isolated instance. Zero coding.

items.label: Available Apps
items.before: Subscribe to separate SaaS for docs, email, KYC, AI, Git, bots, and chat. That's a different vendor, login, and copy of your data for each one.
items.after: Bureau, MerMail, CoinFace, AI Lagoon, BotMother, MiniGit — and more arriving regularly. All Pearls. One OS. Already shipping.

differentiators.heading: Things you literally can't do with SaaS
differentiators.subtitle: These aren't features. They're architectural differences.

features.title: True instance-level isolation
features.description: Not app isolation — instance isolation. Every spreadsheet, photo album, wallet, cap table, and chat room runs in its own container. One client can never see another's. One document can never leak into another.

features.title: No single person can lock you out
features.description: Multi-keyholder approval for vault access, backup decryption, and admin operations. No single point of failure. No single person with all the power.

features.title: Nothing to steal
features.description: Encryption keys exist only when they're needed — created, used once, destroyed. There's no key vault to hack, no password file to steal. Attackers find nothing.

features.title: Revoke access in one action
features.description: Someone leaves? Freeze their Admin NFT — access to everything revoked instantly. No chasing down 12 different service logins. On-chain proof of when it happened.

features.title: AI that genuinely never phones home
features.description: Not 'trust us, we don't look at your data.' Architecturally impossible. The containers have no outbound network access. Your prompts physically cannot leave.

features.title: Verifiable from the outside
features.description: Anyone can check your license on Solana, verify your TLS via DNS, and confirm your code is Foundation-signed. Partners, auditors, regulators — they verify you without trusting you.

features.title: Per-app resource control
features.description: Each container has its own budget. Platform services — OTP, email, AI — deduct micropayments per use. You see exactly what each app costs and set hard limits.

features.title: Connections between specific instances
features.description: A Bureau spreadsheet needs OCR from AI Lagoon. Grapple pops up, you pick a model. That spreadsheet gets AI — nothing else does. A BotMother bot needs to create tickets in MerMail? Grapple connects them. Each connection is between two specific Pearls. Revoke with one click.

features.title: Drag-drop app composition
features.description: Build a client portal by clicking Grapple and picking Pearls: a CoinFace KYC Pearl, a document vault, a chat room. The client sees one unified dashboard. You didn't write any code — you pointed and clicked.

features.title: Accessible from anywhere
features.description: Melusina runs on your server or PC. You reach it from any browser — laptop, phone, tablet. No app to download. No store to approve it. No gatekeeper between you and your own infrastructure.
